water_supply.method: Irrigation water is limited to the renewable water generated locally: annual climatic surplus P - AET from TerraClimate 2011-2020 (mean; year-to-year sd is the uncertainty), 1 mm = 10 m3/ha, taken at ~4 km and compared with each scenario's net irrigation requirement. Effective rainfall is already inside the requirement (net of rain), so no water is counted twice and neighbouring cells are never pooled.
water_supply.evidence: observed climate; supply and deficit are simulated
water_supply.upper_bound: the surplus is an upper bound of locally capturable water (no capture or conveyance losses)
water_supply.reading: High feasibility means the best scenario's water need is met by local renewable water. Where the need exceeds it, feasibility drops and the water deficit (m3/ha/yr) is the amount that would have to come from sources not mapped here.

caveats.ui_banner: Feasibility is water-aware: it assumes irrigation can use only the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km). External water (transfers, fossil groundwater, treated wastewater) is not mapped, so the deficit shown is what would have to come from elsewhere. All outcomes are simulated, none observed.

ece.meaning: weak skill on unseen geography: within-region salinity/sodicity pattern is mostly a regional prior with wide intervals

esp.meaning: weak skill on unseen geography: within-region salinity/sodicity pattern is mostly a regional prior with wide intervals

observed: climate normals and interannual rainfall (TerraClimate 2011-2020, gridded climate product)
crop/ESP/salinity tolerance tables are literature (see expert_rule)
ml_predicted: ECe and ESP (own LightGBM trained on measured WoSIS/Hassani points, conformal intervals)
pH, SOC, texture, coarse fragments, bulk density, CEC (SoilGrids 2.0, third party)
depth to bedrock (SoilGrids 2017, third party, capped 200 cm)
expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)
FAO suitability class boundaries on relative yield (S1>=0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6 [assumed], N<0.4)
simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement

model1_run.confidence_method: Monte-Carlo agreement: share of 24 draws (SoilGrids/SOTWIS/terrain/climate inputs perturbed by documented error models, ML ensemble member and fusion thresholds resampled) that reproduce the central class. It measures robustness to input uncertainty, NOT validated map accuracy.

soilgrids_arid_rmse.note: SOC has no regional skill (R2~0); depth to bedrock capped at 200 cm and uninformative

notes: Areas in equal-area EPSG:6933; 1 dunum = 1,000 m2 = 0.1 ha.
Class 5 (restricted) polygons are never restorable: reported as not_feasible with limiting factor 'restriction'.
All feasibility, post-restoration class, water requirement and time-to-effect values are simulated; none is an observed restoration result.
Feasibility uses the renewable water generated locally (climatic surplus P - AET, ~4 km); water SOURCES (groundwater limits, fossil aquifers, transfers, wastewater, dams) are not mapped.

BATJES_2024.citation: Batjes, N.H., Calisto, L. & de Sousa, L.M. (2024). Providing quality-assessed and standardised soil data to support global mapping and modelling (WoSIS snapshot 2023). Earth Syst. Sci. Data 16:4735-4765.
BATJES_2024.verified_detail: Article landing page read: ~228k profiles, EC (ELCOSP = saturated paste) among standardised properties, per-record licences (CC BY / CC BY-NC / public domain), positional uncertainty ~100 m for 86 % of profiles, purposive (non-probabilistic) sampling.

FAO56.citation: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56.
FAO56.verified_detail: Read ch.3 (Hargreaves eq. 52: ETo = 0.0023 (Tmean+17.8)(Tmax-Tmin)^0.5 Ra), ch.6 Table 11 (stage lengths) and Table 12 (Kc ini/mid/end) rows used in crops.py.

FAO_IDP29.citation: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1.
FAO_IDP29.verified_detail: Read ch.2-3 (HTML): Table 4 crop ECe/ECw yield-potential values (100/90/75/50/0 %), Y = 100 - b(ECe - a) (eq. 10), leaching requirement worked example (ECw 1.2, ECe 2.5 -> LR 0.10; ECe 1.7 -> 0.16), ECe = 1.5 ECw at LF 0.15-0.20, reclamation leaching: 70-80 % (continuous ponding) / 80-90 % (intermittent/sprinkler) salt removal per depth of water equal to soil depth; ECe < 10-12 dS/m needs only 10-20 cm pre-plant irrigation for barley/cotton; gypsum equivalent 86 kg per me/L per 1000 m3.

FAO_SB39.citation: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39.
FAO_SB39.verified_detail: Read ch.4: ESP 15 = sodic limit (Richards 1954), saturation-paste pH 8.2 diagnostic, Table 32 (Abrol 1982) crop ESP tolerance classes (yields seriously affected above ESP ~55 tolerant / ~35 semi-tolerant / ~10 sensitive), Table 33 (Pearson 1960), Table 23 hazard classes, gypsum stoichiometry worked example (0.5 cmol Ca/kg, 15 cm -> 1.96 t/ha pure gypsum).

FAO_SB55.citation: FAO (1985). Guidelines: Land evaluation for irrigated agriculture. FAO Soils Bulletin 55.
FAO_SB55.verified_detail: Read ch.2 and ch.4: land suitability classes S1/S2/S3/N1/N2, relative yield as land productivity index ('top of S2 taken as 80 %, S3 as 60 %'); class-determining factors incl. effective soil depth, stoniness, ESP/salinity, slope, drainage, water supply. The 40 % lower bound of S3 used here is NOT stated in the text (assumption, sensitivity-tested).

FAO_WH91.citation: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91.
FAO_WH91.verified_detail: Read ch.3-4: WATER HARVESTED = CA x design rainfall x runoff coeff. x efficiency; C:CA = (WR - DR)/(DR x K x EFF); K usually 0.1-0.5; EFF 0.5-0.75; design rainfall at 67-75 % exceedance; rainfall variability (mean 200-300 mm: 40-200 % of mean in 19/20 yr; 100 mm: 30-350 %); microcatchment C:CA 2-3:1 guideline.

GRAVUER_2019.citation: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170.
GRAVUER_2019.verified_detail: Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMC6849820): 92 studies in arid/semiarid/Mediterranean rangelands; amendments on average increased soil carbon, water-holding capacity, ANPP; decreased runoff; short study durations (median 1-2 yr). No numeric effect size was read -> used only qualitatively.

HASSANI_2020.citation: Hassani, A., Azapagic, A. & Shokri, N. (2020). Predicting long-term dynamics of soil salinity and sodicity on a global scale. PNAS 117(52):33017-33027.
HASSANI_2020.verified_detail: Dataset record read (Mendeley Data, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.17632/v9mgbmtnf2.1): global ECe/ESP 0-30 cm maps 1980-2018, ~1 km, ML-based; file list/sizes read via public API. Paper not read in full.

MAAS_HOFFMAN_1977.citation: Maas, E.V. & Hoffman, G.J. (1977). Crop salt tolerance - current assessment. J. Irrigation and Drainage Div. ASCE 103(IR2):115-134.
MAAS_HOFFMAN_1977.verified_detail: Crossref record resolved (title, authors Maas/Hoffman, journal, 1977). Numerical thresholds are taken from the FAO_IDP29 Table 4 adaptation, not from the paper.

SWATPLUS_K.citation: SWAT+ Input/Output documentation, 'Soil Erodibility Factor' (equations of Williams, J.R. 1995, EPIC).
SWATPLUS_K.verified_detail: Read the four EPIC factor equations f_csand, f_cl-si, f_orgc, f_hisand (as transcribed in erosion.py). Williams (1995) itself was not read.
